To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
p53 and PKCD are two major players in apoptotic cell death.
PKCδ regulates the expression and function of the tumor suppressor p53 in the apoptotic cell death.
PKCδ is activated by various cellular stresses and regulates p53-dependent and -independant apoptosis in the mitochondria, and p53 binds onto PKCδ promoter to induce its expression upon DNA damages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PKCδ in p53-dependent apoptosis and its implications in cancer treatment.
the molecular mechanism of apoptosis and cancer therapy.
understanding the mechanisms of apoptosis, particularly the intrinsic apoptotic pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53 and PKCD are both important players of the intrinsic apoptotis pathway and they are tightly linked to each other.
the crosstalk and the mutual regulation of p53 and PKCD in the intrinsic apoptotic pathway is an important mechanism to execute the apoptotic machinery in response to various stresses.
the tumor suppressor p53 regulates PKCδ expression and PKCδ regulates p53 expression and function, which together facilitate the execution of apoptotic pathways
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crosstalk of these two tumor suppressors provides a novel therapeutic strategy to treat cancer.
p53 and PKCD are two important tumor suppressor proteins that execute apoptotic pathways in response to various types of cellular stresses.
PKCδ and p53 function in concert to induce apoptosis in response to various stress signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p53 and PKCd cooperate in the regulation of the intrinsic apoptogenic pathways in response to DNA damages and other cellular stresses.
the PKCδ-mediated activation of p53 is critical for apoptosis in response to DNA damaging agents.
PKCδ is not a mere downstream effector of p53; rather, PKCδ and p53 are mutually regulated and cooperate with each other to execute apoptotic pathways in response to cellular stresses.
